title: Last match as a filtered maximum
statement: Let $P\colon\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The last index below $n$ at which $P$ is true, or no value if there is none, equals the maximum of the set of indices below $n$ at which $P$ is true, with the maximum undefined for the empty set.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean-valued predicate on the natural numbers
replaced: For every predicate $P$ and bound $n$, the tracker's candidate below $n$ equals the maximum of the indices below $n$ satisfying $P$; in particular the empty candidate set at time zero is certified.
